item.title: New Attack Bypasses TPM Lockout to Crack Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs in Days, Not Years
item.description: On AMD-based PCs and some Intel PCs, the TPM lockout for Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs can be reset by someone who opens the PC's case, researchers at Technische Universität Berlin say. That leaves short PINs open to guessing. In lab tests, the researchers found a four-digit Hello PIN on an AMD laptop and a 6-digit BitLocker PIN on an Intel laptop this way. item.title: The AI Threat Landscape in 2026: What You Need to Know
item.description: Artificial intelligence is changing cybercrime, but not necessarily by creating new types of attacks. Instead, AI is making familiar threats faster, cheaper, and easier to carry out. Phishing, identity fraud, credential theft, and attacks on software systems can now happen on a much larger scale.
